topics.title: Biology, the microscope and the cell
topics.concept: Characteristics of life, the light microscope, cell theory, cell organelles and transport across membranes.

subtopics.title: Characteristics of living things
subtopics.concept: Metabolism = the sum of all chemical reactions in an organism; other characteristics: growth and development, responsiveness, homeostasis, reproduction (carried out by all organisms, textbook G11 p.25), adaptation.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.1 What is biology? – characteristics of living things

subtopics.title: The light microscope and magnification
subtopics.concept: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification × objective magnification (10× × 4× = 40×).

subtopics.title: Cell theory and cell organelles
subtopics.concept: Cell theory: Schleiden (plants), Schwann (animals), Virchow; Hooke named cells and Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells (Linnaeus founded taxonomy, not cell theory). Ribosome – protein synthesis; mitochondrion – cellular respiration; nucleus – controls cell activities; lysosome – digestion/cleaning; chloroplast – photosynthesis.

subtopics.title: Diffusion and osmosis
subtopics.concept: Osmosis: movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a weaker (dilute) to a stronger (concentrated) solution – it depends on solute concentration.

topics.title: Classification and diversity
topics.concept: Taxonomic ranks, binomial nomenclature, the five kingdoms, viruses, bacteria and animal groups.

subtopics.title: Taxonomic ranks, binomial names and the five kingdoms
subtopics.concept: Kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species; the lower the rank, the more closely related the members. Homo sapiens: Homo = genus, sapiens = species. Protista: simple eukaryotes (protozoa, algae, slime moulds); prokaryotes belong to Monera.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The importance of classification – levels of classification

subtopics.title: Viruses and bacteriophages
subtopics.concept: Viruses have no cells (no nucleus, cytoplasm or membrane) and cannot metabolise or replicate outside a host cell. Lytic cycle: attachment → penetration (injection of nucleic acid) → replication/synthesis → assembly (maturation) → lysis (release).

subtopics.title: Animal groups
subtopics.concept: Tapeworm (flatworm): scolex with hooks and suckers, chain of proglottids. Fishes, amphibians and reptiles are poikilothermic (cold-blooded); birds and mammals homoeothermic. Omnivores eat plants and animals (humans, pigs).

topics.title: Nutrition, photosynthesis and respiration
topics.concept: Biomolecules, vitamins and deficiency diseases, photosynthesis, respiration and fermentation.

subtopics.title: Biomolecules and vitamins
subtopics.concept: Amino acids (building blocks of proteins) all contain an amino group (–NH₂) and a carboxyl group; about 20 occur in proteins. Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy): bleeding gums and mouth, poor healing of wounds, bleeding under the skin, anaemia (delayed clotting is vitamin K deficiency).

subtopics.title: Photosynthesis, respiration and fermentation
subtopics.concept: Light reaction: light → chemical energy, O₂ released. Dark reaction: CO₂ fixed into glucose. Cellular respiration converts the chemical energy of food into ATP in all living cells (plants included). Yeast fermentation releases CO₂, which makes bread rise.

topics.title: Circulation, blood, lymph and immunity
topics.concept: Heart and circulation, plasma and blood groups, lymphatic system and immunity.

subtopics.title: Heart and circulation
subtopics.concept: Pericardium: tough, protective, flexible and elastic membrane that stretches and shrinks with the heart; pericardial FLUID reduces friction. Venae cavae bring body blood to the right atrium. Semilunar valves stop backflow into the ventricles. Systemic circuit: heart → body organs and tissues → heart.

textbook_refs.section: 2.3 Circulation routes – pulmonary and systemic circulation

subtopics.title: Plasma and blood groups
subtopics.concept: Plasma functions: transport of nutrients, fluid/electrolyte balance, favourable pH, globulins (antibodies) fight disease, fibrinogen for clotting. Agglutination = reaction between red-cell antigens (agglutinogens) and plasma antibodies (agglutinins).

subtopics.title: Lymphatic system and immunity
subtopics.concept: Lymphatic tissue: lymph nodes, tonsils, spleen, thymus. Lymph: water, dissolved substances, wastes, absorbed fat, lymphocytes – no red cells. Physical barriers: skin and mucous membranes; chemical defences: tears, mucus, saliva.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1 Components of the lymphatic system; lymphatic tissue
4.1 Innate immunity – physical and chemical barriers

topics.title: Respiratory and excretory systems
topics.concept: Airways and breathing, excretory products and organs.

subtopics.title: Airways
subtopics.concept: The larynx is held open by cartilage; the Adam's apple is a prominent cartilage of the larynx. The epiglottis closes the trachea (glottis) during swallowing so food goes into the oesophagus.

subtopics.title: Excretory organs and products
subtopics.concept: Kidneys: urea, salts, water (urine carries most nitrogenous waste); lungs: CO₂ and water vapour; skin: sweat; liver: breaks down old red cells and makes urea.

topics.title: Nervous system and sense organs
topics.concept: Neurons, synapses, cranial and spinal nerves, the eye and the other sense organs.

subtopics.title: Neurons and nerves
subtopics.concept: Neurons have dendrites, cell body and axon; mature neurons do not divide. The gap between neurons is the synapse. 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves.

textbook_refs.section: 8.3 The peripheral nervous system – spinal nerves

subtopics.title: Sense organs and eye defects
subtopics.concept: Sense organs: eye, ear, nose, tongue, skin. The conjunctiva is the thin transparent membrane covering the front of the eyeball. Long sightedness = hypermetropia (convex lens); short sightedness = myopia (concave lens).

textbook_refs.section: 7.1 The sense organs – introduction; 7.1.1 The skin

topics.title: Endocrine and reproductive systems
topics.concept: Endocrine glands and hormones; reproduction, sexual characteristics and pregnancy.

subtopics.title: Hormones and endocrine glands
subtopics.concept: Main endocrine glands: pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas (islets), thymus, pineal, gonads; the hypothalamus is a brain centre that controls the pituitary. Hormones regulate growth and development, metabolism, the internal environment, sexual function and reproduction. Pituitary GH excess → gigantism. Prolactin (milk production) and oxytocin (milk ejection) act on the mammary glands.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1 The endocrine glands – role of the endocrine system
1.1 The endocrine glands; 1.1.1 hypothalamus and pituitary
1.1.1 The pituitary gland – prolactin and oxytocin

subtopics.title: Sexual characteristics, placenta and umbilical cord
subtopics.concept: Primary sexual characteristics are the genital (reproductive) organs; secondary ones appear at puberty. The umbilical cord (arteries and vein) connects embryo and placenta, bringing food and oxygen and removing wastes.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 Puberty – primary and secondary sexual characteristics

topics.title: Skeletal and muscular systems
topics.concept: Endo- and exoskeletons, the human skeleton, joints and muscles.

subtopics.title: Skeleton and joints
subtopics.concept: The endoskeleton lies inside, under muscles and soft tissues, and grows with the body; exoskeletons limit size, become heavy and must be moulted. Axial skeleton: skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum. Joints: immovable (skull sutures), slightly movable, freely movable – ball-and-socket (hip, shoulder), hinge (knee, elbow), pivot, gliding.

subtopics.title: Muscle functions
subtopics.concept: Muscles move the body and work in breathing (diaphragm, intercostals), digestion (peristalsis) and circulation (heart, vessel walls); the endocrine system works by hormones, not muscle action.

topics.title: Homeostasis
topics.concept: Maintenance of a constant internal environment by feedback: temperature, water and blood sugar.

subtopics.title: Homeostasis, temperature and water balance
subtopics.concept: Homeostasis = maintenance of a constant internal environment. A constant body temperature keeps enzymes at their optimum. Water loss → hypothalamus detects concentrated blood → more ADH from posterior pituitary → more water reabsorbed in the nephrons → blood water rises. Exercise, balanced diet, sleep and rest help homeostasis.

topics.title: Plant systems
topics.concept: Shoot and root systems, tissues, meristems, germination, flowers and transpiration.

subtopics.title: Organ systems, tissues and transpiration
subtopics.concept: A plant has two organ systems: shoot and root. Growing points (apical meristems) are at the tips of stems and roots. Vascular tissue = xylem + phloem. Transpiration: loss of water vapour from a living plant, mainly through the stomata of the leaves.

subtopics.title: Flowers and germination
subtopics.concept: Complete flower: sepals, petals, stamens (anther + filament) and pistil (stigma, style, ovary). The embryo's radicle becomes the root and the plumule the shoot.

textbook_refs.section: 6.3 Sexual reproduction in plants – structure of a flower

topics.title: Nucleic acids and genetics
topics.concept: Nucleotides, transcription and translation, meiosis and Mendelian inheritance.

subtopics.title: Nucleic acids, protein synthesis and meiosis
subtopics.concept: Nucleoside = base + sugar; nucleotide = base + sugar + phosphate. All living things and viruses contain nucleic acids. Transcription: synthesis of RNA from a DNA template (RNA polymerase). tRNA translates the nucleotide (codon) language into amino acids. Meiosis: two divisions, four haploid cells, in all sexually reproducing organisms.

subtopics.title: Mendelian inheritance
subtopics.concept: Aa × Aa → genotypes AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1 (three genotypes); phenotypes 3 dominant : 1 recessive, so 1/4 show the recessive trait.

topics.title: Evolution
topics.concept: Evidence (vestigial organs), Lamarckism, Darwinism, variation and isolating mechanisms.

subtopics.title: Theories and evidence of evolution
subtopics.concept: Darwin: overproduction, variation, struggle for existence, survival of the fittest. Vestigial organs (human appendix) are reduced, generally useless organs – evidence from comparative anatomy.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 Evidence of evolution – comparative anatomy (vestigial organs)

subtopics.title: Variation and isolating mechanisms
subtopics.concept: Genetic recombination (crossing over, independent assortment, fertilisation) creates new combinations; mutation creates new alleles. Isolating mechanisms: behavioural (courtship song), seasonal, habitat, mechanical, gametic/zygotic mortality.

textbook_refs.section: 2.3.4 Sources of genetic variation – genetic recombination

topics.title: Ecology and adaptation
topics.concept: Ecosystems, trophic levels, nutrient cycles, community relations, pollution and adaptation.

subtopics.title: Trophic levels and nutrient cycles
subtopics.concept: Trophic levels: producers, primary consumers (herbivores), secondary/tertiary consumers (carnivores) – decomposers recycle. Carbon cycle: photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion/industry. Oxygen cycle: photosynthesis releases O₂; respiration uses O₂ and returns CO₂ and water.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Intra- and inter-specific relations; pollution
subtopics.concept: Intra-specific: co-operation, competition, division of territory, hierarchy. Inter-specific: predation (most significant), parasitism, competition between species. Acid rain comes from air pollution (SO₂ and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels).

textbook_refs.section: 3.1 Ecosystem – human impact on the environment

subtopics.title: Adaptation
subtopics.concept: Adaptations are inherited and increase fitness; strategies: escape, avoidance, tolerance. Xerophytes: sunken stomata, reduced leaves, thick cuticle, extensive roots; buoyant leaves belong to hydrophytes.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 4 – Plants, Animals and the Environment
